text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - Bunds traded near unchanged levels from Tuesday's close after recovering from the day's low at 102.75. Analysts see the possibility of consolidation but expect no major sell-off. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 103.23, up 0.32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts ended up with modest gains, not a bad performance given early losses of a half-point and more, dealers said. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 113-24/32, up 14/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures closed stronger but well off the highs they set earlier in the day and PIBOR futures turned negative in afternoon trading, weighed on by a slightly weaker dollar. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 131.76, up 0.12 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Debt markets made a half-hearted bid for the upside by the end of trade but volumes were low and dealers said clients were not convinced. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 131.18, up 0.36 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - The prices of U.S. government securities were narrowly mixed in light trading at midday ahead of the 10-year note sale, the second leg of the Treasury's quarterly refunding auction. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 112-20/32, up 05/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.69 percent.

JAPAN - Key March Japanese government bond futures ended the session lower in thin trade, following a rise in Tokyo stocks and the yen's fall against the dollar. In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.22, down 0.12 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - A $1.0 billion deal for Credit Local during the morning headed primary market activity which included more euro Eurobonds, this time from Societe Generale. The Credit Local deal was a seven-year offering at an 18 b.p. spread, a level seen as aggressive. Societe Generale launched bonds in French francs and marks which will be redenominated in euros after EMU. Other activity included retail-targeted deals in dollars, Australian dollars, lire and marks.
